contributions.statement: After an agent generates code from a structured spec, run a completeness pass that maps every spec element (actor, precondition, flow step) to a design element and every design element to a code symbol by AST lookup, and feed each missing link back to the agent for at most about three repair rounds; removing this pass cut judged coverage from 54.8% to 39.9% and test success from 47.2% to 28.4%.
contributions.evidence: §3.5 Algorithm 2 and §5.2 Fig. 8 ablation. Single run, eTour plus DeepSeek-V3.2 only. Coverage is judged by DeepSeek-V3.2 and success counts only judge-passed tests. The pass also adds LLM rounds (no compute-matched control). Requirement-to-design links are LLM-asserted and never scored, and code nodes are whole files.
relative_to: 2605.15846 give every spec target its own acceptance test (missing implementation about 29% of failures)

contributions.statement: Before design or code generation, have the agent normalise each use case into a fixed schema (actor, entry/exit conditions, numbered steps) with an explicit subject in every step and a parser check that forces regeneration on violations; without this step test success fell from 47.2% to 28.3%.
contributions.evidence: §3.2 and Fig. 8: no-Refiner ablation, success 47.19 -> 28.27 and coverage 54.78 -> 43.13. Single run, one dataset and model. The Refiner infers missing subjects instead of asking, so for domain rules a guessed actor is a risk that this setup never measures.
relative_to: 2608.09072 spec templates should state constraints and verification explicitly
2609.22259 state default and wildcard encodings explicitly in specs

contributions.statement: Have the agent emit a class and sequence design (for example PlantUML) from the spec before writing code; without it, output collapsed from about 15 files to 5 and test success fell from 47.2% to 36.8%.
contributions.evidence: Fig. 8 no-Designer ablation, single run on eTour with DeepSeek-V3.2.
relative_to: 2608.19854 planner emits a requirement-to-component map and dependency graph before code, +7.6-29.7 pp with stronger evidence

contributions.statement: Keep an execute-and-repair loop on agent-generated code; without the tester's run-tests-and-fix rounds, success fell from 47.2% to 13.9%.
contributions.evidence: Fig. 8 no-Tester ablation, single run. Tests are written by the same pipeline from the use case and generated code.

reason: The traceability-completeness loop and use-case normalisation are plausible, transferable refinements, but each rests on one single-run ablation scored by a judge from the generating model family, with link accuracy never measured. They remain hypotheses. The design-first and test-loop findings duplicate or restate stronger KB evidence.
